cheese_maker.text: Cheddar is the world's most popular cheese for a reason. It comes from this village and it's always sold out.
Tradition says to turn the cheese by hand every day. After thirty years, my wrists have opinions.

caver.text: Cheddar Man was found in Gough's Cave in 1903. About 10,000 years old, and Britain's oldest complete skeleton.
In 1997 a local history teacher turned out to share his DNA. Very distant cousin. Not a bad ancestry quiz.

climber.text: Jacob's Ladder: 274 steps up to the clifftop. I do them twice every morning. Then I eat an entire cheese roll.
The gorge is up to 137 metres deep. Don't look down. I'm joking. Look down. It's brilliant.

goat_watcher.text: Peregrines, ravens and, if you're very lucky, a feral goat in an impossible spot.
Soay sheep live up there too. They're an ancient breed. The oldest thing on the cliffs, apart from the cliffs.

berry_picker.text: The Cheddar Valley was famous for strawberries. They rode out on the 'Strawberry Line', a railway built for them.
Now it's a walking and cycling path. You can still smell the jam on a warm day.

goat.text: It chews. It stares. It has decided you are not a threat, and not a snack either.
